title: Serverless web app
summary: A static front end plus an API with no servers to manage — the classic modern starter architecture.

steps.text: Users resolve your domain (app.example.com) through Route 53, which points it at CloudFront with an alias record.
CloudFront serves the site from edge locations close to users and forwards /api calls to API Gateway.
The single-page app's HTML, JS and images live in a private S3 bucket that only CloudFront may read (Origin Access Control).
Users sign in through a Cognito User Pool and receive a JWT to send with every API call.
API Gateway validates the Cognito token, applies throttling and invokes the backend.
Lambda runs the business logic per request — it scales to zero and you pay per invocation.
DynamoDB stores the data with millisecond reads at any scale; on-demand mode removes capacity planning.
CloudWatch collects Lambda logs and metrics so you can alarm on errors and latency.

title: Classic three-tier app
summary: Load balancer, auto-scaled servers and a managed database spread across Availability Zones.

steps.text: A Route 53 alias record points your domain at the load balancer.
An Application Load Balancer in public subnets terminates HTTPS and spreads requests across several AZs.
Web and app servers run on EC2 in private subnets — unreachable directly from the internet.
Security groups chain the tiers: the app tier only accepts traffic from the load balancer, the database only from the app tier.
An Auto Scaling group adds instances under load and replaces unhealthy ones automatically.
RDS Multi-AZ runs the relational database with a synchronous standby in a second AZ for failover.
ElastiCache keeps hot reads and user sessions in memory to offload the database.
A NAT Gateway lets private instances download patches without being reachable from outside.

title: Event-driven processing
summary: Decouple producers from consumers so each piece scales and fails independently.

steps.text: A user uploads a file to S3.
S3 emits an "Object Created" event to EventBridge, where rules match on bucket and prefix.
SQS buffers the work so traffic spikes never overwhelm consumers; failed messages land in a dead-letter queue.
Lambda polls the queue in batches and scales the number of consumers automatically.
Multi-step jobs run as a Step Functions workflow with retries, branching and waits — no glue code.
The workflow records results and job status in DynamoDB.
SNS notifies users and downstream systems when the job finishes.

title: Data lake & analytics
summary: Stream raw data into S3, catalog it, then query it ad hoc or in a warehouse.

steps.text: Clickstream or IoT events stream into Kinesis Data Streams in real time.
Kinesis Data Firehose lands the raw data in an S3 data lake, partitioned by date.
Glue crawlers infer schemas into the Data Catalog; Glue jobs clean the data and convert it to Parquet.
Athena runs ad-hoc SQL directly on S3 using the catalog — you pay per terabyte scanned.
Curated data is loaded into Redshift for fast, repeated BI dashboards.
Macie scans the lake for personal data so it can be masked or locked down.

title: Container CI/CD
summary: From git push to a running container, with safe, gradual deployments.

steps.text: A push to the main branch starts CodePipeline.
CodeBuild runs the tests and builds a Docker image.
The image is pushed to ECR and scanned for known vulnerabilities.
CodeDeploy starts a blue/green deployment, shifting traffic to the new version gradually.
ECS launches tasks from the new image and keeps the desired count healthy.
Tasks run on Fargate — no EC2 instances to patch or scale.
CloudWatch alarms watch the new version and can trigger an automatic rollback.

title: Hybrid & multi-VPC network
summary: Connect a data center to many VPCs through one hub instead of a mesh of links.

steps.text: A dedicated Direct Connect link carries steady, high-volume traffic from the data center.
A Site-to-Site VPN over the internet adds an encrypted backup path that can be up in minutes.
Transit Gateway is the hub: on-premises links and every VPC attach once, and route tables decide who talks to whom.
Each workload gets its own VPC attached to the hub — isolated by default, connected on purpose.
Workloads sit in private subnets spread across Availability Zones.
Network ACLs add a stateless subnet-level filter on top of security groups.

title: Account security baseline
summary: Guardrails, audit trails and threat detection every AWS environment should start with.

steps.text: Organizations groups accounts; Service Control Policies set guardrails no one in an account can exceed.
IAM roles grant least-privilege, temporary access — no long-lived access keys.
An organization trail records every API call in every account to a central S3 bucket.
Config tracks how resources change over time and flags anything that breaks your rules.
GuardDuty analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs for threats like crypto-mining or leaked keys.
Findings flow to EventBridge to alert the team or trigger automated remediation.
KMS keys encrypt data at rest across S3, EBS, RDS and more, with every key use logged.
